Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: The grandparent learns that a family member is dealing with a significant personal crisis.
Expectation2: Secure packages and confirm successful delivery
Situation2: Leaving a package safely at the doorstep when no one is home
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was pulling up to the next house on my delivery route. It was a message from my daughter: “Grandpa, can you call? Mom’s not doing well.” My heart clenched. I knew my daughter needed me, especially now, when things at home were so fragile. As a grandparent, I always promised to be there, to listen, to offer comfort. But as I looked at the package in my hands, I remembered the strict instructions from my supervisor—every delivery had to be confirmed, every package left in a secure spot, no exceptions. The house in front of me was empty, no one answering the door, and the neighborhood wasn’t the safest. I could feel the weight of both roles pressing down on me: my family needed my voice, my presence, but my job demanded my attention and care for the package. I stood on the porch, phone in one hand, package in the other, torn between the call I needed to make and the delivery I needed to complete.
